blogs.title: When a Young Patient’s Blood Sugar Doesn’t Fit the Ordinary Diabetes Puzzle
blogs.description: This post walks clinicians through the tell‑tale clues that should raise suspicion for MODY – early‑onset hyperglycaemia, a dramatic family history, glycosuria without ketoacidosis, and a non‑obese phenotype – and how a simple clinical algorithm can flag candidates for genetic testing.

blogs.title: Decoding the HNF1A Gene: From Novel Mutation to Targeted Therapy
blogs.description: Explore the mechanics of the HNF1A transcription factor, why mutations in its DNA‑binding domain are so deleterious, and how a newly identified p.N270S variant exemplifies the spectrum of pathogenic HNF1A changes driving MODY.

blogs.title: Glucagon‑Stimulated C‑Peptide Re‑Considered: A Practical Guide for the Emergency Room
blogs.description: Focuses on the role of the glucagon test in distinguishing residual β‑cell function, its interpretation thresholds, and how results influence the switch from insulin to oral agents or GLP‑1 agonists in suspected MODY patients.

blogs.title: Sulfonylureas vs GLP‑1 Agonists in HNF1A‑MODY: When Hypoglycaemia Is Your Biggest Fear
blogs.description: A comparative discussion of first‑line sulfonylurea therapy versus newer GLP‑1 receptor agonists, including evidence from crossover trials, patient‑centred outcomes like hypoglycaemia risk, weight changes, and long‑term β‑cell preservation.

blogs.title: SGLT‑2 Inhibitors in HNF1A‑MODY? An Unintended Danger Zone
blogs.description: Delve into the biology of SGLT‑2 under HNF1A control, the paradoxical dehydration and ketoacidosis risk in HNF1A‑MODY, and why clinicians should think twice before prescribing these agents in monogenic diabetes.

blogs.title: From Gene Panel to Clinical Practice: How Next‑Generation Sequencing Is Changing Diabetes Care
blogs.description: Illustrates the practical workflow of using NGS panels for MODY screening, the ACMG interpretation framework, billing considerations, and how finding a pathogenic variant can shift a patient from insulin to tailored oral or injectable therapies.
